title: Office of the President's proposed P10-B budget breezes through Senate plenary
summary: The Senate plenary on Tuesday afternoon quickly approved the proposed P10 billion budget of the Office of the President (OP) for fiscal year 2027 in two minutes.

blocks.text: The Senate plenary on Tuesday afternoon quickly approved the proposed P10 billion budget of the Office of the President (OP) for fiscal year 2027 in two minutes.
Budget sponsor Senator JV Ejercito noted that the recommended new appropriations for the OP now amounts to P10,083,518,000.
Senate Majority Leader Juan Miguel Zubiri then moved to terminate the deliberations on OP’s budget “out of courtesy.”
Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente “Tito” Sotto III approved the motion with no objections.
Executive Secretary Ralph Recto was present in the session hall for the plenary debates.
Under the 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP), the OP originally sought a total of P10,155,758,000 budget, about 64% lower than the 2026 budget.

Recto previously said the substantial reduction reflected the "lower operational requirements of [the OP's] delivery units and the completion of activities related to the Philippines' hosting of the ASEAN Summit for which no additional funding will be required next year."
"In short, we're asking for less while remaining fully prepared to do more," Recto said the House Committee deliberations into OP’s proposed 2027 budget.
"We believe this amount is sufficient for the Presidency to meet the exacting demands of leading the nation at a time of overlapping domestic and external challenges," he added. —NB, GMA News
